Lucia — great to connect. Quick recap and next steps below.

Recap (short):
- Redwood showed routing, KV prefix caching, and dedicated capacity options.
- Our runtime supports continuous batching and hardware-aware kernel selection which reduces cost per token for long-running sessions.

Per-1M token comparative snapshot (baseline assumptions: mixed prompt+generate 50/50, avg output 200 tokens, steady-state warm kernels):
- Redwood Hosted (default high-throughput): $18 / 1M tokens (no dedicated commitment)
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, 1 node equivalent): $11 / 1M tokens (includes smart batching/caching)
- AWS Bedrock (public endpoints, estimated): $28 / 1M tokens (varies by model family + egress)
- Google Vertex Inference (estimated): $24 / 1M tokens
- Self-hosted on G5-like (our modeled infra + ops): $14–$20 / 1M tokens (high variance, excludes ops overhead)

Notes on batching & cache:
- Batching improves throughput; effective per-token CPU/GPU cost decreases with larger batches but increases P95.
- Prefix/KV cache hit rates are the biggest lever for seq-gen workloads:
  * 10% cache hit -> ~baseline costs above
  * 40% cache hit -> ~20–30% reduction in per-token cost
  * 70% cache hit -> ~45–60% reduction in per-token cost (depends on prompt lengths)

Hyperscaler comparison notes:
- Cold-start P95: hyperscalers have aggressive scale-to-zero behavior leading to higher P95s on bursty traffic; Redwood Dedicated can pin capacity for consistent P95
- Compliance/procurement: we support private deployments and custom SLAs for Dedicated/Private plans — happy to share our standard SOW and SLA language.

Attachments: cost estimate workbook (redwood-cost-estimate-1Mtokens.xlsx) and a proposed test harness spec.

Proposed next tests (short):
1) 48-hour throughput run to measure cost @ 3 cache-hit profiles (10/40/70%)
2) Latency P95 test with steady-state and cold-start bursts
3) Token-mix sensitivity (vary avg output 50 / 200 / 800 tokens)

Can we lock a 2-hour slot May 19–20 for initial warm-up + qualifiers? Markus (sales lead) and Tessa (SE) are looped to help provision and run the test harness.

Thanks — I will also upload an expanded TCO sheet and the test spec to the Drive link.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Test plan + measurable success criteria for May 19–20 window

Hi Lucia / Alyssa — thanks for aligning on dates. Below is the test plan and exactly what we will measure.

Summary: 48-hour continuous run covering three cache-hit profiles and three token mixes. Goal: provide deterministic per-1M token cost numbers + P95 latency and throughput curves.

Environment & infra:
- We will run Redwood Dedicated trial (2 nodes) in us-west-2.
- We will provide an API key scoped to the trial and a small workload generator (python harness) you can run from your infra or ours.
- If you prefer private peering for egress accuracy, request VPC peering by May 15.

Workloads (each run ~12 hours):
1) Mix A (low output): prompt-heavy, avg response 50 tokens, target throughput 50 req/s
2) Mix B (medium): avg 200 tokens, target throughput 25 req/s
3) Mix C (long): avg 800 tokens, target throughput 5 req/s

Cache-hit profiles: 10%, 40%, 70% (we'll seed prefix cache to simulate each profile).

Metrics collected:
- Per-1M token cost (raw infra cost + Redwood platform overhead)
- P50/P90/P95 latency (end-to-end)
- Batch size distribution and effective GPU utilization
- KV cache hit ratio and token-savings impact
- Failure/retry rate and tail error analysis

Quick example numbers (expected ranges) based on similar customers:
- Redwood Hosted baseline: $18 / 1M tokens @ 10% cache. With 40% hit -> $13.5 / 1M. With 70% hit -> $8.5 / 1M.
- Redwood Dedicated modeled: $11 / 1M @ 10% hit, $8.5 / 1M @ 40% hit, $5.5 / 1M @ 70% hit.
- Hyperscaler roughs: $24–28 / 1M (limited batching control + higher P95 for bursty traffic).

Deliverables after run (within 48 hours):
- Cost breakdown workbook with assumptions + raw telemetry
- Latency/throughput graphs and a short 1-page executive summary comparing Redwood vs hyperscaler baselines

Action items before May 15:
- NovaScale: confirm whether you will run the harness from your infra or want us to run it (reply to this thread)
- NovaScale: share any procurement timing or special compliance items to surface ahead of trial
- Redwood: Jasmine to provision trial, Tessa to seed cache and provide scripts, Markus to confirm discount path if needed

Attachment: novascale-test-harness-spec.md (script list, env vars, seeding instructions).

Looking forward — we will kick off provisioning once you confirm the harness run location.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
